Classify the draws of a csfmt_ensemble_v4 into MEM intensity levels

Source: R/v4_mem.R
mem_thresholds_v4.Rd

Fits Moving Epidemic Method (MEM) thresholds for each season from the earlier seasons of the same series, and classifies every draw against them. The method is that of mem_thresholds_v1() for a csfmt_ensemble_v3, and the values are identical.

Usage

mem_thresholds_v4(
  x,
  measure,
  min_seasons = 2,
  prefer_seasons = 5,
  i.seasons = 10,
  min_weeks_per_season = 30,
  exclude_seasons = NULL
)

Arguments

x

The csfmt_ensemble_v4, full or compressed.

measure

The name of the draw matrix to classify, a count or a rate. It MUST NOT end in a reserved suffix.

min_seasons

The fewest training seasons for a fit.

prefer_seasons

A fit on fewer training seasons is provisional.

i.seasons

The most training seasons in one fit, passed to mem::memmodel().

min_weeks_per_season

The fewest weeks that a training season needs.

exclude_seasons

Seasons to leave out of every training set, written as cstime::isoyearweek_to_season_c() writes them, such as "2019/2020". An excluded season still gets thresholds, and a message names the excluded seasons in the data.

Value

x with the new draw matrix <measure>_mem, which holds the level codes 1 to 5 with a levels attribute. It adds these columns to $data:

  • <measure>_mem_thr_preepidemic, <measure>_mem_thr_medium, <measure>_mem_thr_high and <measure>_mem_thr_veryhigh: the thresholds of the season of the week.

  • <measure>_mem_n_seasons: the number of training seasons of the fit.

  • <measure>_mem_prob_preepidemic to <measure>_mem_prob_veryhigh: the share of the draws at each level, which is NaN when every draw is NA.

The shares give every ordinal percentile of the level codes, so the step writes no percentile column.

Each new name MUST be at most 63 bytes. A rerun on the same measure replaces the draw matrix and the columns. The input x does not change.

Details

The fit uses the median of the draws of each week. A season is fit only on earlier seasons: those with at least min_weeks_per_season weeks, minus exclude_seasons, and at most the latest i.seasons. The seasons and the season weeks come from the ISO weeks in x$time_col.

A season gets no thresholds, and NA in every draw, in three cases:

  • it has fewer than min_seasons training seasons;

  • fewer than 2 of them hold a week above 0;

  • mem::memmodel() fails with its default method and with i.method = 3.

A fit on fewer than prefer_seasons seasons is provisional, and a message counts those seasons.

The levels, coded 1 to 5, are:

  1. preepidemic: below the MEM epidemic threshold.

  2. low: below the 40% intensity threshold.

  3. medium: below the 90% intensity threshold.

  4. high: below the 97.5% intensity threshold.

  5. veryhigh: at or above the 97.5% intensity threshold.

The function draws no random numbers. It needs the mem package. The function takes no ..., so a misspelt argument is an error.

See also

Other v4 functions: as_ensemble_v4(), csfmt_ensemble_v4(), csfmt_reporting_triangle_v4(), ens_add_rate_v4(), ens_compress_v4(), nowcast_ecdf_v4(), nowcast_passthrough_v4(), print.csfmt_ensemble_v4(), short_term_trend_v4(), signal_detection_hlm_v4()

Examples

# MEM needs earlier seasons, so this series spans four: 212 weeks with a
# winter peak in each.
if (requireNamespace("mem", quietly = TRUE)) {
  w <- cstime::dates_by_isoyearweek$isoyearweek
  iyw <- w[match("2018-30", w) + 0:211]
  lam <- 20 + 60 * exp(-(cstime::isoyearweek_to_seasonweek_n(iyw) - 25)^2 / 40)
  set.seed(1)
  ens <- csfmt_ensemble_v4(
    data.table::data.table(location_code = "nation", isoyearweek = iyw),
    id_cols = "location_code",
    draws = list(cases = matrix(rpois(212 * 50, lam), nrow = 212))
  )
  ens <- mem_thresholds_v4(ens, measure = "cases")
  ens$data[
    isoyearweek %in% c("2021-45", "2022-02"),
    .(isoyearweek, cases_mem_thr_high, cases_mem_prob_high)
  ]
}
#> mem_thresholds_v4: 3 season(s) fit on < 5 training seasons (provisional); see cases_mem_n_seasons.
#>    isoyearweek cases_mem_thr_high cases_mem_prob_high
#>         <char>              <num>               <num>
#> 1:     2021-45           82.29283                   0
#> 2:     2022-02           82.29283                   0
